In [[mathematics]], the term '''Beurling algebra''' is used for various different algebras introduced by {{harvs|txt=yes|first=Arne|last=Beurling|authorlink=Arne Beurling|year=1949}}. Usually it is an algebra of [[periodic function]]s with [[Fourier series]]

:<math>f(x) = \sum a_n e^{inx}</math>

'''Example'''
We may consider the algebra of those functions ''f'' where the [[majorant]]s

:<math>c_k = \sup_{|n| \ge k} |a_n|</math>

of the  Fourier coefficients ''a''<sub>''n''</sub> are summable.  In other words

:<math>\sum_{k \ge 0} c_k < \infty.</math>

'''Example'''
We may consider a weight function ''w'' on <math>\mathbb{Z}</math> such that
:<math>w(m+n) \leq w(m)w(n),\quad w(0)=1,</math>
in which case <math>A_w(\mathbb{T}) = \{f : f(t) = \sum_n a_n e^{int},\,\|f\|_w = \sum_n|a_n|w(n) < \infty\} \,(\sim\ell^1_w(\mathbb{Z}))</math>
is a [[unitary group|unitary]] [[commutative]] [[Banach algebra]].

These algebras are closely related to the [[Wiener algebra]].
